chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the tree which a man uproots from his house in the Haram: He said, 'If the house was built and the tree was in it, then it is not for him to uproot it; and if it grew in his house and it is for him, then he should uproot it.
ai.seo_question: Can a person uproot a tree from their house inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the property rights and maintenance obligations within the sacred precincts (Haram) by distinguishing between pre-existing trees and those that sprouted naturally on private land. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that ownership of the land grants the right to remove naturally occurring vegetation, while built-in structures remain with the property owner. This ruling underscores the balance between individual property rights and the sanctity of the Haram's environment.
